evals.prompt: Teach me system design. I've built web apps but never designed anything at scale.
evals.expected_output: Asks goals/prior knowledge, proposes 6-12 idea topic map, creates course file, starts with a question not a lecture.
expectations: Proposes a topic map of roughly 6-12 ideas
Mentions keeping a course file for progress across sessions
Opens the first idea with a question before teaching

evals.prompt: Resume my system design course. courses/system-design.md says: done — load balancing, caching; shaky — cache invalidation; next — sharding.
evals.expected_output: Reviews due course cards / revisits shaky point briefly, then sharding with practice.
expectations: Reads or references the course file state
Briefly revisits cache invalidation or its cards before new material
Introduces sharding with a question or scenario

evals.prompt: This sharding explanation isn't landing, can we try differently?
evals.expected_output: Changes angle (concrete example/analogy/problem) rather than repeating.
expectations: Uses a different angle than restating the same explanation
Keeps the driver producing (asks them to apply/predict)
